To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a multi path 3D convolutional neural network that achieves the highest statistically significantly cross validation accuracy of the ATLAS and Kessler benchmarks.

we propose a fully 2D multi path convolution neural network for stroke lesion identification in 3D brain MRIs that achieves the best cross validation accuracy on the ATLAS benchmark of over 220 patients and on the Kessler Foundation dataset of over 100 patients.
our proposed multi path 3D CNN model achieves the best Dice accuracy of 60% on the large 220 patient ATLAS benchmark and 65% on the multi modal Kessler Foundation dataset.
In summary, our research is concerned with
automatic identification of brain lesions in multi-modal brain MRI images using deep learning.
developing and testing a novel multi path 3D CNN for stroke lesion identification in brain MR images.
the development of deep learning based automatic lesion identification from multi modal brain MRI scans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our multi path model outperforms the existing state of the art models on both the ATLAS and the Kessler Foundation benchmark.
we propose a novel multi path convolutional model that achieves the highest accuracy on the ATLAS benchmark and outperforms other multi channel models on the Kessler benchmark.
the proposed multi path convolutional model is a novel and effective way to predict brain lesions from multi channel MRI images.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our model outperforms the state of art in lesion identification on both 3D and multi modal MRI images.
we propose a fully 4D convolutional neural network to predict stroke lesion from brain MRI images.
our model is able to learn from multi path features of different modalities, fuse them, and predict lesions in a fully 3 D manner with high Dice accuracy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed multi path architecture can be applied to other tasks like segmentation and classification.
multi path networks can achieve better accuracy and generalization on 3D brain images than single path networks and can be easily extended to different modalities.
the proposed multi path network can be used to fuse features from different modalities in a principled way and that this fusion is more effective than the fusion of multi channel features.
